page.title: Trained reinforcement learning agents across algorithm families and environments.
page.description: Thirteen agents built while completing the Hugging Face Deep RL Course, covering tabular Q-learning, policy gradients, DQN, PPO (Stable-Baselines3, from-scratch PyTorch, and Unity ML-Agents), A2C, multi-agent self-play, and asynchronous RL with Sample-Factory.

section.heading: Published models
section.description: Each agent was trained, evaluated, and published to the Hugging Face Hub while completing the Deep RL Course.

items.title: PPO · LunarLander-v3
items.label: PPO
items.summary: Trained with 16 parallel environments and evaluation callbacks to preserve the best checkpoint. Mean reward: 302.83 ± 17.47 across 100 episodes.
items.note: Uses parallel rollout collection and periodic evaluation - closer to how production RL training is structured than a single-environment loop.

items.title: DQN · SpaceInvaders
items.label: DQN
items.summary: Deep Q-network trained on raw pixel frames from Atari SpaceInvaders, with frame stacking and standard Atari preprocessing.
items.note: Shows how value-based deep RL handles high-dimensional pixel inputs without explicit feature engineering.

items.title: Huggy · Unity ML-Agents
items.label: PPO (Unity ML-Agents)
items.summary: PPO agent trained in a Unity environment where the agent learns to run toward a thrown stick using the ML-Agents toolkit.
items.note: Demonstrates how RL extends beyond standard Gym environments into custom simulation setups with continuous action spaces.

items.title: REINFORCE · PixelCopter
items.label: REINFORCE
items.summary: Policy gradient agent trained on PixelCopter, a continuous state environment where the agent controls altitude to pass through gaps.
items.note: REINFORCE learns directly from full episode returns - a clean implementation of the core policy gradient idea before adding baselines or actor-critic structure.

items.title: REINFORCE · CartPole-v1
items.label: REINFORCE
items.summary: Policy gradient agent trained to balance a pole on a cart. A clean baseline for verifying a REINFORCE implementation before moving to harder environments.
items.note: CartPole's fast convergence makes it useful as a sanity check - if the policy gradient loop is wrong, it will fail visibly here.

items.title: Q-Learning · Taxi-v3
items.label: Q-Learning (tabular)
items.summary: Tabular Q-learning agent trained on the Taxi environment: pick up a passenger and drop them at the correct location in a 5x5 grid.
items.note: Tabular Q-learning stores the full Q-table explicitly, which is tractable for small discrete environments like Taxi but breaks down as state space grows.

items.title: Q-Learning · FrozenLake
items.label: Q-Learning (tabular)
items.summary: Tabular Q-learning agent trained on the deterministic (no-slip) version of FrozenLake - navigate from start to goal without falling in a hole.
items.note: The no-slip variant removes environment stochasticity, making it a cleaner case for learning Q-values from a fixed transition model.

items.title: PPO · Pyramids (Unity ML-Agents)
items.label: PPO (Unity ML-Agents)
items.summary: PPO agent trained in the Pyramids environment, where the agent must find a switch, press it, then locate the pyramid it reveals - a sparse-reward task with no signal until the sequence is completed correctly.
items.note: Sparse rewards make naive exploration fail; Unity ML-Agents' PPO setup here relies on curiosity-driven exploration to discover the rewarded sequence at all.

items.title: PPO · SnowballTarget (Unity ML-Agents)
items.label: PPO (Unity ML-Agents)
items.summary: PPO agent trained to throw snowballs at a moving target in a custom Unity ML-Agents environment.
items.note: First custom (non-Gym) Unity environment in the course progression - establishes the ML-Agents training/export workflow used again for Pyramids and Huggy.

items.title: A2C · PandaReachDense-v3
items.label: A2C
items.summary: Advantage Actor-Critic agent trained on a simulated Panda robotic arm to reach target positions in 3D space, using the dense-reward variant of the task. Mean reward -0.19 ± 0.07 across evaluation episodes.
items.note: A2C's combined actor-critic update generalizes cleanly from discrete Gym control to a continuous, multi-dimensional robotics action space.

items.title: POCA · SoccerTwos (Unity ML-Agents)
items.label: POCA (multi-agent)
items.summary: Multi-agent POCA (MA-POCA) agents trained to play 2v2 soccer against each other through competitive self-play, coordinating with teammates while adapting to an opposing team that improves over time.
items.note: Multi-agent training breaks the single stationary environment assumption behind most RL algorithms - the opponent's policy keeps shifting as it learns, so the agent has to keep adapting rather than converging against a fixed target.

items.title: PPO (from scratch) · LunarLander-v2
items.label: PPO (custom PyTorch)
items.summary: PPO implemented from scratch in PyTorch - clipped surrogate objective, GAE, and the actor-critic update written manually rather than via Stable-Baselines3. Trained for 1M timesteps across 8 parallel environments; mean reward 122.65 ± 50.04.
items.note: Reimplementing PPO's internals (clipping, advantage estimation, value loss) builds a working understanding of the algorithm that using a library alone doesn't - a direct complement to the SB3-based LunarLander-v3 agent above.

items.title: APPO · ViZDoom Health Gathering Supreme
items.label: APPO (Sample-Factory)
items.summary: Asynchronous PPO agent trained with Sample-Factory 2.0 to navigate a ViZDoom level and collect health items while avoiding damage. Mean reward 11.45 ± 3.40.
items.note: Sample-Factory trains with asynchronous, high-throughput rollout collection rather than SB3's synchronous loop - the same class of infrastructure used for large-scale RL research.
